newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates up in tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates up in tight liquidity.

text.p: * Drained by investments in dollars, securities
Philippine interbank call loan rates jumped to an average of 12.00 percent on Tuesday from 11.71875 in a tight market after banks invested in dollars and government securities, traders said.
"The Central Bank sold dollars to banks. That translates to pesos out of the system," a dealer said. The Central Bank sold over $100 million on Tuesday and $56.5 million on Monday.
Done rates ranged from 12.75 percent to 11.0625.
Market volume was higher at 23.394 billion pesos from 20.938 billion. Out of the 62 participating financial institutions, 38 were lenders.
Banks bought dollars after foreign funds withdrew their investments in securities due to falling interest rates.
At the same time, banks had also locked in their money in the fixed-income bills ahead of the expected further slide in interest rates.
In the secondary market for T-bills, banks were trying to sell their bills to generate liquidity but there were not many takers due to the tight liquidity situation, a dealer said.
